html_en:
The biggest story in AI today isn't a new model — it's a new mental model: Claude has joined the Slack workspace, and the industry is reckoning with what it means when AI stops being a tool you visit and starts being a colleague you manage.

🧵 The Third Paradigm: Claude Joins the Team

Anthropic launched Claude Tag in beta today for Slack Enterprise and Team customers, and the reaction from builders has been striking — less "cool feature," more "this changes everything."

Andrej Karpathy framed it with characteristic precision:

"This is the 3rd major redesign of LLM UIUX. The first paradigm was that the LLM is a website you go to, the second was that it is an app you download to your computer. This third one is that it is a self-contained, persistent, asynchronous entity with org-wide tools and context, working alongside teams of humans. It really takes a while to wrap your head around it, but it works and it is awesome."

The mechanics, explained by Anthropic engineer Boris Cherny, are deliberately sandboxed and surgical:

"Tag Claude in a channel, it spins up an instance with its own sandbox. It clones repos, writes code, tests, compiles — all in that isolated environment — and the sandbox gets thrown away when it's done. One instance per thread, its own memory and permissions per channel."

Anthropic's Cat Wu noted that this isn't just an external product — it's already reshaped internal shipping: "Our internal version merges 65% of product PRs and this is our first product that is natively multi-player and proactive." The official rollout post and a breakdown of six common workflow configurations are worth bookmarking.

Alex Albert put it simply: "This has completely changed how I work with Claude. It feels less like using a tool and more like managing a team."

Thomas Roquilly shared a set of practical orchestration tips — having Claude maintain a pinned status message in your personal channel, react to threads with emoji status indicators (⏲️✅❓🛑), even act as a scheduling assistant that books calendar time on request.

🧠 When AI Becomes a Colleague, What Is Design?

The Claude Tag launch surfaces a deeper philosophical question that Peter Yang posed with elegant simplicity:

"What is design if what's accessing your product is just an agent looking for an API or CLI?"

It's not rhetorical. The same day, the internet erupted over a viral tweet from @steipete: "Google fired the guy that made the Google Workspace CLI, because he made the Google Workspace CLI." The post landed nearly 4,000 likes — a Rorschach test for how the industry feels about large companies resisting the agent-native future. Yang himself noted the Google Workspace CLI is "super useful and should be celebrated."

Aaron Levie connected the dots to Box's own play, describing Claude Tag as an example of "headless software": "With Claude Tag, you can give Claude access to any corporate files in Box that you can interact with from Slack. Now all of your enterprise content becomes a portable knowledge base."

💰 The Token Pricing Wars: Where Does Value Accrue?

Beneath the product launches, a quieter but consequential debate is intensifying around AI pricing strategy. @realmadhuguru, who has observed the ecosystem from multiple vantage points, offered a sober read:

"The core tension here is that the business models, moats, value exchange, execution playbooks for all players are being figured out in real time. This debate around token pricing is really a debate over where value will accrue — models, application layer, distribution or other layers. Expect a lot of strong opinions from the different sides to shape the narrative in their favor."

Levie offered a sharper thesis: a barbell is emerging between expensive frontier models and cheap-but-capable open weights alternatives — and the "applied AI layer" wins by routing intelligently between them. "The closer you are to the underlying workflow, the better you can tune the use of models for a given business process." That means domain-specific evals, customer-level fine-tuning, and deep data infrastructure — not just prompt engineering.

🧬 Zuckerberg's Moonshot: Open-Source Biology at Scale

Away from the Slack integrations and pricing debates, No Priors dropped a fascinating episode featuring Mark Zuckerberg, Priscilla Chan, and Alex Rives on the Chan Zuckerberg Biohub's evolution into a full-scale AI-for-biology initiative. Watch/Listen: Biohub: The Future of Biology is Open-Source

The $500M "virtual biology initiative" is premised on a belief that accelerating science requires not just AI models, but entirely new datasets that don't yet exist — requiring new imaging tools, cellular engineering, and measurement devices built from scratch. Zuckerberg explained the original insight:

"Unlike language models, there's just a lot of data out there on the Internet. That's not really the case with biology... You wanna be able to visualize things that people haven't been able to see before. You want to be able to record things that are going on inside the body. Or you want to be able to measure things like inflammation in ways that haven't been possible."

The open-source commitment is strategic, not just idealistic. As Zuckerberg put it: "We'll have a bigger impact by getting this in more scientists' hands quicker by doing it as open source projects." The Biohub network — now spanning San Francisco, New York, and Chicago — has already folded over 1.1 billion proteins and built tools like CellxGene that spawned their own research communities. The ambition: world models of cells, then whole biological systems. The original goal of curing all disease by century's end, once mocked by Nobel laureates, now strikes Zuckerberg as "too conservative."

⚡ Quick Signals

  • Vercel + Cursor: Guillermo Rauch teased a Vercel/Cursor integration and is recruiting high-signal agent builders into a private feedback group for eve engineers.
  • OpenAI Codex bugs: @thsottiaux at OpenAI has been publicly triaging Codex bugs in real time on X — the most refreshingly transparent bug-fix thread of the week, landing 3,200+ likes.
  • NotebookLM in classrooms: Josh Woodward shared a quote from Florida State University: "Shortly after introducing NotebookLM on campus, we watched students who were struggling with a 'C' grade completely transform their study habits and their grades in a matter of weeks."
  • GLM goes global: Swyx hyped Zhipu AI's ascent — from obscure GLM models to what some are calling the world's top open model, with a Hong Kong IPO and a return to SF for AI Engineer Summit.
html_zh:
今天的头条属于一个产品：Claude Tag正式登陆Slack，重新定义了人与AI协作的边界——与此同时，扎克伯格夫妇押注开源生物学，试图用AI重写人类对疾病的理解。

🤖 Claude走进办公室：AI协作的第三次范式革命

今天最重要的发布毫无疑问是Claude Tag——Anthropic将Claude直接嵌入Slack工作流，面向Enterprise和Team用户开放测试。这不只是一个功能更新，而是一次关于"AI应该如何存在于工作中"的深层重构。

Andrej Karpathy 罕见地给出了高度评价，并将其定位为LLM交互界面的第三次重大演变：

第一个范式是：LLM是一个你去访问的网站；第二个是：它是你下载到电脑上的应用。第三个是：它是一个自包含的、持久的、异步的实体，拥有组织级别的工具和上下文，与人类团队并肩工作。真正理解这一点需要一些时间，但它确实有效，而且令人惊叹。

Anthropic内部产品负责人 Cat Wu 透露，这款产品已在内部改变了他们的研发流程：

Claude Tag是我们在Anthropic发布产品方式的范式转变。我们的内部版本合并了65%的产品PR，这是我们第一个原生多人协作且主动出击的产品。

产品的技术实现细节同样令人印象深刻。工程师 Boris Cherny 描述道：在频道中@Claude后，它会启动一个独立沙盒实例，克隆代码库、编写代码、测试编译，完成后沙盒销毁——每个线程一个实例，每个频道有自己的记忆和权限。他还设置了Claude主动监控Slack频道、回答问题、起草PR，并用✅❌等表情符号标记线程状态。

Anthropic的 Tommy Reddad 则分享了使用心得：当任务变多时，可以让Claude在置顶消息中实时更新所有任务的状态，用⏲️✅❓🛑表情一目了然地显示进度。还有人正在搭建"日程安排"频道，让同事@Claude来协调日历。

Box CEO Aaron Levie 看到了更大的图景：

这是"无头软件（headless software）"与智能体结合的又一范例。通过Claude Tag，你可以让Claude访问Box中所有企业文件，从Slack就能调用。你的全部企业内容因此成为一个可携带的知识库。

Anthropic的 Alex Albert 一句话点破了用户感受："这完全改变了我与Claude的工作方式。感觉不像在使用工具，更像在管理一个团队。"

🔧 工具即战场：CLI的反叛与代理时代的设计哲学

就在Claude Tag发布的同一天，一个关于Google Workspace CLI的小插曲在开发者圈引发广泛共鸣。Peter Steinberger 发帖称：

Google解雇了那个做Google Workspace CLI的员工，因为他做了Google Workspace CLI。幸运的是，Google解雇不了我。

这条推文获得近3700个赞，成为今日最高互动之一。Peter Yang 也感叹："Google Workspace CLI超级有用，应该被表彰。"

这场讨论背后是一个更深的问题，Peter Yang随后抛出了一个发人深省的设计命题：

如果访问你产品的只是一个在寻找API或CLI的智能体，那设计还有什么意义？

他还观察到人机交互正在演变为"管理一名高能力员工"——"要不要给Claude安排一对一面谈和绩效评估？😅"

🧬 扎克伯格的另一场赌注：用AI重写生物学

Watch/Listen: No Priors: Biohub: The Future of Biology is Open-Source

如果说Meta是扎克伯格的商业战场，那Biohub是他与Priscilla Chan共同押注的文明级实验。在No Priors播客中，两人详述了这项五亿美元"虚拟生物学"计划的起源与野心。

一切始于十年前一系列"有趣的尴尬对话"——他们带着"治愈所有疾病"的宏大目标去拜访诺贝尔奖得主，结果被当场嘲笑。最终科学家们告诉他们，真正的障碍是：研究各自为政、数据封锁、工具无法共享传承。一个博士后在实验室电脑上做出的好工具，毕业后就消失了。

我们不认为我们会是治愈疾病的人。我们的目标始终是构建工具，加速整个科学领域的进步，这样科学界集体就能治愈所有疾病。——Mark Zuckerberg

如今，Biohub已折叠超过11亿个蛋白质结构，并在纽约、芝加哥等地建立了多个分中心。其核心逻辑是：生物学数据不像语言模型的训练数据那样唾手可得，必须从头发明新的科学方法来生成。从单细胞测序到细胞成像，从炎症测量设备到整个生物系统的世界模型，Biohub正在试图为AI提供训练生物学大模型所需的底层数据基础设施。

Zuckerberg坦言，当年认为"本世纪末治愈所有疾病"是过于乐观，现在反而觉得太保守了。

💰 模型定价之战：价值将在哪一层沉淀？

AI产业的另一条暗流是商业模式的根本性不确定性。投资人 Madhu Guru 直言不讳：

围绕token定价的争论，本质上是一场关于价值将在哪里积累的争论——是模型层、应用层、分发层，还是其他层？各方都会强力输出有利于自己的叙事。

Box的Aaron Levie对此有清晰的判断：市场将形成"哑铃型"结构——高成本前沿模型与廉价但够用的开源/闭源权重模型两端并存。真正的竞争发生在中间的应用层：谁能最懂具体工作流、做好领域评估、管理好代理所需的数据，谁就能从中套利。

与此同时，GLM模型的崛起也在重塑格局。Shawn Wang（swyx）兴奋地写道，智谱AI已IPO，并在某些评测中超越了DeepSeek，"毫无争议地成为世界顶级开源模型"——这场开源模型的竞赛远未结束。
